about: The project's milestones, for Charts/Project Chronology (`beta/chronology.html`, written into its `chronology-data` slot by `beta/chronology_page.py` when the site is published).

Operator 2026-11-28: "add a project chronology to charts/ at the end for now. post the important milestones along a timeline. show the progress we've made. ai capability, simulator performance, new features, other".

A milestone is `date` (the UTC day it happened), `category` (a key of `categories`), `title`, `detail` (one or two sentences, every figure in them dated) and `sources`, where a reader can check it. `major` marks the few the timeline names on the chart itself, each by its short `label`.

`progress` is the row of figures over the timeline, each a before and an after: `label` (what was measured), `was` and `now` (the two readings), `span` (the days they were read on) and the `category` whose colour it wears. Each restates milestones below it.

A source is one of: `pr` (a pull request number), `commit` (a commit on main, for the first days, before pull requests), `ledger` (a game's tag on the ledger branch, under `runs/`), `data` (a file in this repository), `video` (a YouTube address) or `release` (a release tag). `says` is what the link reads as; without one the page words it from the kind.

Dates are UTC days: a game's is the day its result was recorded (`utc` on its line of `results.jsonl`), a pull request's or commit's the day it reached main. A milestone that sums a stretch of days is dated on the stretch's last day.

`beta/chronology_page_test.py` holds every milestone to this shape and checks the ones that restate a file in this repository against that file (`docs/civ6_ladder.json`, `data/performance/*.json`, `data/tournaments.json`). A figure read off the ledger branch says so in `checked` and names the day it was read: the ledger is not in this tree, so no test here can read it again.
To add a milestone, add a line here in date order. The page needs no other change.
checked: The ledger figures (first wins, weekly Deity records, game counts) were read off `results.jsonl` on the ledger branch as it stood at 2026-11-28T06:43:27Z, counting a game once by its best run as `tools/live_status.py` does. The commit count is `git rev-list --count main` at 6daa2053 the same day.

categories.name: AI capability
categories.says: How well the CIVVIS AI agents play, measured in Civilization VI itself against the game's own AI.

categories.name: Simulator performance
categories.says: How fast the simulator plays a game, and how many games one machine gets through.

categories.name: New features
categories.says: What a visitor or a player can do that they could not do before.

categories.name: Other

progress.label: Highest level beaten in Civilization VI
Wins against the Lv 8 Deity AI

milestones.label: Project starts
milestones.title: The project starts
milestones.detail: The first commit is civ65 v0.1, a headless engine in the style of Civilization VI. It is renamed CIVVIS the same day.

milestones.title: A Rust core on day one
milestones.detail: The engine begins in Python, gets a Rust core at v0.3 and is pure Rust at v0.6, all on the first day.

milestones.title: Watch a game in the browser
milestones.detail: Spectator mode: every seat is played by the AI and the game is drawn in a browser page the engine serves.

milestones.title: Strategies are rated, bred and gated
milestones.detail: Within two days the AI strategies have an Elo rating from games against each other, a genetic loop that evolves their weights, and a statistical gate a new champion has to pass.

milestones.title: Planet maps and single player
milestones.detail: A globe of hexagons and twelve pentagons, a True Start Earth on it, and a game you start and play from the browser.

milestones.title: Public, and built by a fleet of AI agents
milestones.detail: The repository is public by this day, and a collaboration policy checked on every pull request keeps many AI coding agents working on one trunk.

milestones.label: Plays the real Civ VI
milestones.title: CIVVIS takes a seat in the real Civilization VI
milestones.detail: Computer control lands: a mod and a harness let the agent play a seat of Firaxis's own game. The first run on the ledger lasts 23 turns.

milestones.title: One game across many cores, the same game
milestones.detail: A deterministic executor runs a game's AI phases in parallel without changing the game that gets played.

milestones.label: civvis.ai live
milestones.title: civvis.ai goes live
milestones.detail: The site publishes the browser build of the simulator and the downloads.

milestones.title: v0.6.0, the first release
milestones.detail: The engine as one self-contained program for Windows, macOS and Linux, to download and run offline. v0.6.1 follows on 2026-08-07.

milestones.title: Two lanes: a promoted site and a test site
milestones.detail: civvis.ai serves a build that was promoted on purpose, while a second lane follows main as it changes.

milestones.title: The same seed makes the same world on every build
milestones.detail: Globe geometry goes through one maths library, so map generation is bit-identical across builds.

milestones.title: First win against Civilization VI's own AI
milestones.detail: At Lv 1 Settler, in a game played the full 250 turns: the first win on the ledger, 18 days after the first run.

milestones.title: The gene screen
milestones.detail: A change to how the AI plays ships as a gene that can be switched on or off, and one batch of games with random genomes prices every gene at once. Six days later the screen publishes its first 5,000-game batch.

milestones.title: Up the ladder to Lv 4 Prince in a week
milestones.detail: First wins at Lv 2 Chieftain (08-18), Lv 3 Warlord (08-22) and Lv 4 Prince (08-23), each over the full 250 turns.

milestones.title: First win at Lv 5 King
milestones.detail: Rome, a Science victory on turn 234, six players on Continents.

milestones.title: First win at Lv 6 Emperor
milestones.detail: Rome again, a Science victory on turn 213.

milestones.title: The 1,000th game against Civilization VI
milestones.detail: Counting finished games on the ledger since the first on 2026-07-31. The 5,000th follows on 2026-11-20.

milestones.title: The baseline: ten minutes a self-play game
milestones.detail: In a batch of 3,480 six-player games played from 10-09 to 10-15, the median game takes 630 s, 2.9 s a turn.

milestones.title: First win at Lv 7 Immortal
milestones.detail: Greece, a Diplomatic victory on turn 194 on a four-player Pangaea. The first on six-player Continents follows on 11-03: Korea, Science, turn 198.

milestones.label: First Deity win
milestones.title: First win at Lv 8 Deity
milestones.detail: Korea, a Science victory on turn 205 against five Deity AIs on Continents, 81 days after the first win at Lv 1.

milestones.title: A whole game in 52 seconds, on video
milestones.detail: The site plays a complete game in real time, 199 turns to a Science victory. The record falls to 14 seconds two days later.

milestones.title: Deity beaten four ways
milestones.detail: After Science: a Diplomatic victory (11-06, turn 172), a Religious one (11-10, turn 175) and a Culture one (11-16, turn 179).

milestones.title: First hot seat game against a person
milestones.detail: CIVVIS's flagship agent plays three seats of a real Civilization VI Hot Seat game against the project owner.

milestones.title: A self-play game in under two and a half minutes
milestones.detail: In a batch of 3,862 games played from 11-15 to 11-18 the median game takes 139 s, 0.66 s a turn: 4.5 times faster than October's, after dozens of changes that each play the same games in less time.

milestones.title: The AI Debugger
milestones.detail: A timeline to step back along, jump on and set breakpoints on, then a screen split into two simulators.

milestones.title: Tournaments begin
milestones.detail: Series of games against the Lv 8 Deity AI, each with its own record. The first is ten games and one win.

milestones.title: A whole game in under 6 seconds
milestones.detail: Four players on a Tennis Ball map at Online speed, start to victory, on video. The record was 9 seconds on 11-17.

milestones.title: Deity wins stop being rare
milestones.detail: The week of 11-09: 1 win in 340 Deity games on six-player Continents. The week of 11-16: 46 in 385, or 12%.

milestones.title: The official benchmark starts
milestones.detail: One CIVVIS agent against five of the game's AI at Lv 4 to Lv 8, played whenever no tournament is running. Its win rate at each level is the project's primary benchmark.

milestones.title: Games per minute: 18 on one machine
milestones.detail: A new benchmark counts the self-play games finished in a minute with a worker on every core: 18.3 on an 18-core M5 Max. In the newest batch of games, played from 11-21 to 11-22, the median game takes 93 s.

milestones.title: Charts/
milestones.detail: Win Analytics and CIVVIS Performance open a Charts/ section on the site. AI Interpretability, ELO Rankings, Civ Analytics and AI Insights join it within three days.

milestones.title: Autosearch
milestones.detail: The AI Debugger searches for a line of play that meets conditions you set: what you need, must avoid, want and don't want.

milestones.title: Doctor Strange's CIVVIS
milestones.detail: One world, two timelines: the same game played two ways, side by side, on a timeline that branches.

milestones.title: Fog-honest by default
milestones.detail: The AI seats on the site decide from what a player in their seat could see, and nothing behind the fog.

milestones.title: 24 games a minute: 35,000 a day
milestones.detail: The same benchmark two days on: 24.3 games a minute on one machine, 7,299 times the pace of a person playing a five-hour game by hand.

milestones.title: CIVVIS: Edge of Tomorrow
milestones.detail: You play one civilization, with a jump back: the world returns to the turn you woke on, as it stood.

milestones.title: What the browser costs: 1.7 times
milestones.detail: One game played both ways, same seed, same 130 turns: 17.0 s on the native program and 29.5 s on the site's WebAssembly build.

milestones.label: Playable in Civ VI
milestones.title: Playable in your own Civilization VI
milestones.detail: Hot seat becomes something to hand to a player: a cover hides CIVVIS's turns, you set the game up yourself, and the mod does nothing without its program running. Setup steps reach the README the next day.

milestones.title: People on the Elo list
milestones.detail: A hot seat duel played under your name is rated among the agents on ELO Rankings.

milestones.title: MIT licence
milestones.detail: CIVVIS's own code goes under the MIT licence, with notices for the work of others it carries and a statement that it is a fan project. It was GPL from 2026-08-02 until the licence was taken off for review on 11-25.

milestones.title: CIVVIS: Moneyball
milestones.detail: A minigame of numbers only: pick a player strategy by its stats, ten turns at a time.

milestones.title: Deity at even odds
milestones.detail: Since 11-22: 59 wins in 340 Deity games, 17%, where an even seat among six would take 16.7%. Lv 4 Prince stands at 41 of 41. Tournament 8, a hundred Deity games with the Diplomatic victory off, ends 21 to 79.

milestones.title: Pull request 6,000
milestones.detail: 130 days in, main holds 6,290 commits. Pull request 2,000 merged on 08-18 and 4,000 on 10-09.
